name: straight_block_prints
why: The term of comparison of the overhangs, and it is half of the criterion of the entry: «on a known vertical face, supported». A straight block has nothing that overhangs: four vertical walls (0 degrees of overhang), the top face looking up, and the bottom one resting on the plane.
_why_the_bottom_face_does_not_count: It looks straight down: 90 degrees of overhang, the worst possible case. But it rests on the plane of the machine and prints perfectly well. Counting it would mean declaring unprintable EVERY existing part -- and it is the easiest way to write a check that is good for nothing. It is counted apart, in `area_resting_on_plane_mm2`.

expect.tolerance_why: two faces of 100x100 and four of 100x20: the calculation is exact, but the area is summed by the tessellation

expect.why: THE LINE THAT SAYS THE PLANE WAS RECOGNISED. Without it this number would be zero and `faces_overhanging` would be one: the most trivial block in the world would come out unprintable.
the limit is declared at every call: a short horizontal crossbar prints all the same, and this operation does not know it
